title: Matrix entry
parts: The entry of A in row i and column j.
example: For A with rows (2,5) and (7,9), a₁₂ = 5.
wrong: The entry in row j and column i.
The product of entries i and j.

title: Matrix transpose
parts: The matrix formed by swapping the rows and columns of A.
example: A single row [1, 2] becomes the column with entries 1 and 2.
note: Aᵀ rearranges entries. A⁻¹ reverses a linear map when the inverse exists.
wrong: The matrix obtained by negating every entry of A.

title: Determinant of a matrix
parts: The determinant of the square matrix A.
example: For the diagonal matrix with entries 2 and 3, det(A) = 2 × 3 = 6.
note: A determinant can be negative. These bars do not ask for an absolute value.
wrong: The number of rows of A.
The sum of the diagonal entries of A.

title: Matrix rank
parts: The dimension of the column space of A.
example: The columns (1,2) and (2,4) span a line, so rank(A) = 1.
note: Counting columns gives the rank only when the columns are independent.
wrong: The number of columns, whether independent or not.

title: Kernel or null space
parts: The set of vectors v for which Av is the zero vector.
example: For A = [1 0], every vector of the form (0,t) is in the kernel.
note: The kernel describes inputs that map to zero, rather than outputs produced by A.
wrong: The set of all vectors produced as Av.
The set of columns of A.

title: Inner product
parts: The inner product of vectors u and v, a scalar.
note: The angle brackets denote the product, rather than the angle between the vectors.
wrong: The vector from u to v.
The angle between u and v in degrees.

title: Euclidean norm
parts: The Euclidean length of vector v.
note: The subscript 2 names the norm. It does not square the length.
wrong: The square of the Euclidean length of v.

title: Eigenvector and eigenvalue
parts: Applying A to nonzero v gives
the same vector scaled by λ.
example: For A = diag(2,3) and v = (1,0), Av = 2v, so λ = 2.
note: The zero vector is excluded even though A0 = λ0 for every λ.
wrong: A changes the direction of v by the angle λ.
λ is the number of coordinates of v.
